overview.summary: Liino is a 6★ Electric Supporter wielding a Polearm. Her kit combines team healing, ATK bonuses, SP refunds and Electric/Nature amplification. Her gameplay revolves around two stances and setting up a strong Ultimate buff window for the rest of the squad.
strengths: SP recovery through her talent and Combo Skill interactions.
Versatile support across numerous team compositions.
Straightforward gameplay without highly technical execution.
weaknesses: Her signature weapon is particularly important for achieving maximum team amplification.
Golden Age is a viable Battle Pass option but noticeably weaker as a dedicated buff weapon.

operatorKit.playstyle:
Liino supports her team through two successive stances. Dazzling Focus costs 25 SP and activates Vocalist Stance for up to 60 seconds. While active, the team gains an ATK Boost (10% at M3), allies in range receive ongoing HP Treatment, and nearby enemies are periodically hit with additional Electric DMG. When an Arts Reaction is applied or consumed during the stance, Liino's Combo Skill, Delightful Harmonics, heals the controlled operator, restores 20 Ultimate Energy and keeps Vocalist Stance active. Her combat talent, Starry Boost of 1st Magnitude, can then refund up to 10 SP on the next Electric or Nature Battle Skill used within 30 seconds at the highest talent rank.

Dawnstar Concerto costs 160 Ultimate Energy and activates the stronger Cosmovoice Stance for 15 seconds, granting an ATK Boost and Electric Amp / Nature Amp that further scale with Liino's Will. It also heals allies in range, deals Electric DMG and applies Electrification across a large area. The normal end of Cosmovoice Stance releases a final beat with triple damage and healing. Using Liino's Battle Skill again while either stance is active ends the stance prematurely; this also prevents Cosmovoice's normal finishing effect. Align her Ultimate with your team's most important damage window and avoid ending her stance by accident.

active.basic: Leave at level 1. Liino takes on the role of a supporter here; Additional levels in the Basic Attack do not significantly benefit their team reinforcement, SP refund and Ultimate rotation.
active.battle: M3 is the goal because the Battle Skill grants 10% ATK bonus to the team. Their amplification values increase with the skill levels. Between this skill and the combo skill, the investment order is flexible, as both are aimed at M3.
active.combo: Also on M3. The cooldown drops from 10 to 8 seconds according to official skill data. The more frequently Liino can trigger her combo skill through matching arts reactions, the more often she receives the constant 20 Ultimate energy and the more often her combat talent can refund a subsequent electric or nature battle skill with up to 10 SP after the combo. The SP comes from the talent, not directly from the combo itself.
active.ultimate: Highest priority, M3. Liino’s strongest team benefit is the Will-scale electro/nature amplification of Ultimate. On M3, the additional amp reaches 0.04% per will point, with a maximum contribution of 60% from Will. The actual gain achieved depends on the desired value.

recommendations.evaluation: Liino's best-in-slot rod weapon. Bedazzling Night debut combines Will for their Ultimate amp with an additional ATK amplification for team members treated by Liino.
Golden Age is the Battle Pass option. She delivers Will as well as Arts damage amplification through Liino’s healing combo skill. Their modeled performance depends on the team.
JET is the alternative rod weapon for Liino. It delivers its own damage and attribute effects instead of replacing the specific Team ATK effect of its BiS weapon.
Cohesive Traction is the F2P option. It has suitable will values, but its weapon effect is more focused on own electric/combo skills damage than on additional direct team reinforcement.

teams.introduction: Liino takes on the support role in every compilation shown here. Electric and nature teams in particular benefit from their Ultimate, while the long-lasting general ATK bonus of their Battle Skill also enables other team compositions.

conclusion.verdict: Liino is a strong general pull recommendation and a valuable support for almost any account. Her Ultimate is particularly effective at amplifying Electric and Nature teams, while the very long-lasting, general ATK Boost from her Battle Skill also makes her attractive in many other team compositions. Once her Battle Skill is active, she can support the team mostly passively, without requiring complex coordination with other abilities.
recommendedFor: Generally a strong option for almost every player.
Especially helpful when prioritizing Electric or Nature teams.
Also useful in many other team compositions beyond the examples listed.
skipIf: Check your existing roster first. If there is genuinely no support slot she improves, skipping is reasonable.

overview.summary: Typhoeus (Typhi) is a 6★ Nature Striker using an Arts Unit and playing as an active main DPS. Her strongest attacks are empowered aerial shots that trigger Nature Bursts. Nature Infliction stacks prepared by her teammates increase that damage and generate Signs for additional Hunting Arrows. She can hit two enemies at once, but her rotation, positioning and SP economy are demanding.
strengths: High Nature Burst damage through empowered aerial shots, especially when Nature Infliction stacks are prepared.
Targets up to two enemies at once while Hovering.
Both her Combo Skill and Ultimate can reset aerial attack attempts and extend the rotation.
Strong synergy with Arcane or Fluorite as a reliable Nature Infliction source.
weaknesses: Very limited team flexibility: reliable Nature Infliction setup generally requires Arcane or Fluorite.
Her Battle Skill costs 100 SP and her Ultimate can require 200 energy; Final Strikes and SP timing matter.
Being interrupted while Hovering loses valuable empowered shots; the protective barrier can break.
Her signature weapon has a substantial advantage over alternatives.

operatorKit.playstyle: Typhi’s entire gameplay revolves around two resources: Signs and Hunting Arrows. The Hunting Arrows are their ammunition for power shots, while signs are converted into new Hunting Arrows in a 2:1 ratio via their combo skill. A maximum of eight signs and four hunting arrows are possible. At the highest level of her combat talent loot checklist, she begins with four signs; Outside of combat, their Hunting Arrows fill up again. Start a fight with four Hunting Arrows if possible. With her Battle Skill (100 SP) Typhi goes into the hovering and can carry out five air attacks. If an attack consumes a hunting arrow, it becomes an energy shot and forces a Nature Burst on hit – even without a previous nature stack. When an airstrike hits an enemy with nature attachment, it consumes a stack and gives a sign and twelve ultimate energy. The Nature Burst generated in this way gives a further sign via loot checklist; An energy shot at an opponent with an existing nature stack can thus deliver two signs. The Nature Burst of this hit also receives the bonus for a consumed stack. With active control, the fifth air attack always counts as a final strike and as an energy shot, but does not consume a hunting arrow. When reaching eight signs, the combo skill can be activated: It exchanges the signs for four Hunting Arrows, resets Typhi’s air attack sequence, and creates a barrage line in which enemies are slowed down, continuously suffer natural damage, and receive increased nature burst damage. The maximum combo cooldown improvement is 19 seconds; It is therefore not an arbitrarily repeatable reset within a single short sequence. Their Ultimate consumes 200 energy, immediately gives two Hunting Arrows, puts them back into the hovering, resets the air strikes and adds one hail of arrows per hit; The fifth hail of arrows is strengthened. This is a strong additional window, but the core of their damage remains the repeated triggering and amplification of Nature Bursts through well-prepared energy shots. Therefore, prepare nature stacks before the damage window, do not waste battle skill and combo too early and plan for SP generation between the hovering phases. In hovering, Typhi receives a protective barrier with up to 30% damage reduction thanks to her second combat talent. A hit can break them; At the highest talent level, it can only be reactivated after 18 seconds. Therefore, watch out for enemy attacks and use Dodge Cancels after the normal Final Strike and after landing to continue the attack sequence faster.

active.basic: Typhoeus's normal Basic Attack consists of five Nature DMG hits. The Final Strike deals 17 Stagger and is particularly important for restoring SP when she is not Hovering. If necessary, use a Dodge Cancel after the Final Strike to shorten its long ending animation. Her normal Basic Attack is not the primary source of damage, so level it last.
active.battle: Top priority and an eventual M3 target. Piercing Arrows of the Woods initiates Hovering for 100 SP, allowing up to five aerial attacks against up to two targets. Hunting Arrows empower these attacks and trigger Nature Bursts. A Burst consumes existing Nature Infliction stacks on the target, increasing its damage; each consumed stack also grants one Sign and 12 Ultimate Energy. The fifth aerial attack also counts as a Power Shot and Final Strike even without ammunition. Skill upgrades are particularly valuable for the Nature Burst multipliers.
active.combo: Second priority and an eventual M3 target. At eight Signs, Rampant Thorns restores four Hunting Arrows, resets the aerial attack sequence and creates a barrage zone that slows enemies and increases their sustained Nature Burst damage. At M3, its cooldown falls to 19 seconds. Line up the renewed aerial attack window with prepared Nature Infliction stacks: the Combo Skill reset alone does not create those stacks.
active.ultimate: Level after the Battle Skill and Combo Skill. At 200 Ultimate Energy, Call of Ice Mountain deals a strong initial hit, provides two Hunting Arrows, resets Hovering and grants five more aerial attacks. The fifth barrage is particularly powerful. In optimized damage windows, using her Battle Skill shortly beforehand can trigger her signature weapon effect in time. The Ultimate extends her empowered-shot rotation; it is not the only reason her Nature Bursts deal so much damage.

combatTalents.evaluation: The most important basic talent for the complete rotation: Nature Bursts provide signs that are converted into Hunting Arrows. At the third talent level, Typhi starts with four signs instead of just one, and the attack amplified by Hunting Arrows gets a factor of 1.6. With enemies exploding at the same time, the nature burst trigger counts according to the official text only once for the sign generation.

The protective barrier helps to play the hovering completely. At the highest talent level: 30% less damage as long as the barrier lasts and 18 seconds reactivation time after it is broken. It is not permanent interruption protection.

shipTalents.evaluation: Growth rate of rare minerals in the growth chamber. irrelevant for combat rotation; The actual values and unlock levels are from the official Talents table.
Increases the growth of fungal material in the growth chamber. An economic/base bonus, not a reason for a particular team composition.

recommendations.evaluation: Umbra of Frigid Eventide is by far her most appropriate weapon. In addition to Agility and ATK, Typhi gets 15 seconds of Arts intensity and four Windform stacks when using the Battle Skill. The subsequent Nature Bursts through energy shots consume these stacks and increase their further Arts damage values. Therefore, especially for boss rotations, place the battle skill immediately before the planned hovering and ultimate burst.

Suffering's End is the meaningful battle pass alternative. The properties fit significantly better with a nature DPS scaling on agility than many older arts units. However, it lacks the signature weapon’s custom-made windform buffs; it is an alternative, not an equivalent BiS option.

Detonation Unit is theoretically playable as an emergency solution. However, their effect is not as precisely matched to Hunting Arrows and Nature Bursts as the Signature weapon or Suffering's End. Only consider if the two better weapons are not available.

builds.title: Build A – Deep Rampart + LYNX Slab
builds.metaSummary: Standard endgame: three parts Deep Rampart for Arts damage and intensity, plus LYNX Slab for more agility and general damage.
builds.teamContext: The general standard for most boss and multi-goal battles; also in the Nefarith and Echo rotations shown a robust choice.
builds.evaluation: Deep Wall (Deep Rampart) is tailor-made for Typhis Nature Bursts: three set parts provide arts intensity and matching damage reinforcements. The LYNX Slab as the fourth part brings a wider value for its entire damage rotation. Base attacks, air strikes, combo, ultimate and nature bursts thus benefit in different proportions. Exactly this setup is the standard recommendation, not just a theoretical DPS tip.
builds.setBonusNotes: 3x Deep Rampart for the set bonus; 1x LYNX Slab as Off-Piece. No second set effect by a single LYNX part.
builds.craftingNotes: Armor, gloves, a Comms and a LYNX Slab require four manufactured parts. Reaching level 70 does not automatically confirm possession of the templates; The build finder checks blueprints, region, components and levels separately.

builds.title: Build B – Deep Rampart with second Comms
builds.metaSummary: For particularly large Nature Burst numbers: second Deep Rampart Comms instead of LYNX Slab, with a narrower focus on Arts explosions.
builds.teamContext: For showcases where maximum individual nature burst values are more important than universally slightly higher total damage.
builds.evaluation: Instead of the LYNX Slab, a second Deep Rampart Comms can be used. This comparison is not a blanket performance jump: The nature bursts can be stronger, while the LYNX variant usually performs better outside of these explosions (normal hits, air strikes, combo and ultimate). In the original 1:1 counterpart, the total distances were small. Decide if you want larger burst numbers or the more balanced standard damage.
builds.setBonusNotes: Furthermore, only the 3 set bonus of Deep Rampart; the fourth part does not trigger a second set bonus.
builds.craftingNotes: Two manufactured comms need two items, but the same unlocked blueprint; The finder counts possession and manufacture accordingly.

builds.title: Build C – More Ultimate Energy with LYNX Cuirass
builds.teamContext: Special rotation with increased demand for Ultimate energy. Only use if an important Ultimate window actually enables earlier.
builds.evaluation: The conditional Ultimate Energy variant from my Mobalytics Guide uses LYNX Cuirass T1, Deep Rampart Gauntlets and twice Deep Rampart Comms. It deliberately dispenses with the Deep Rampart Armor part of the general standard build and is not a blanket recommendation for every fight. The decisive factor is whether the concrete rotation requires additional ultimate energy. The alternative is not only because of the 200 energy automatically above the standard.
builds.setBonusNotes: Two Deep Rampart Comms and Deep Rampart Gauntlets activate the three parts of the set. LYNX Cuirass T1 is the off-piece.
builds.craftingNotes: Both comms must be produced as two separate parts. Check construction plan ownership, materials and actual story availability separately.

builds.teamContext: Transition to Wuling as soon as the corresponding concrete templates are actually activated.
builds.evaluation: AIC Fieldwork Assault Armor, Assault Gloves and Assault Push Knife combine main attributes with arts intensity. The AIC Fieldwork Ember complements Ultimate Energy Profit. Thus, the set supports the combination of agility, nature bursts and repeated air phases until Deep Rampart is reachable.

builds.evaluation: The roving MSGR combination of jacket, fists, flashlight and gyro puts agility at the forefront. This fits directly with Typhi’s main attributes and is a clean intermediate stage before the Arts intensity of later Gear.
builds.craftingNotes: All four parts and their level limits are verified from the official item catalogue.

teams.introduction: Typhi should always be played with at least one team member who can reliably build up nature stacks. Arcane in the Will variant is the strongest and most flexible partner: nature attachments, grouping and matching buffs combine to form a meaningful burst rotation. In the Will build, Arcane should reach at least 640 Will after the original game example to exhaust their relevant buffs. Fluorite is the particularly good alternative if arcane is missing or additional nature stacks are needed. The remaining two slots should buff, heal or enable reactions as much as possible without blocking Typhi’s tight SP budget. Ardelia and Perlica can trigger suitable reactions for Liino's combo; Gilberta is an alternative with group support, Xaihi strengthens nature teams. Antal and Purrchena bring situational possibilities. Prepare nature stacks for all teams before power shots and actively reclaim the 100 SP for the Battle Skill with Final Strikes.

meta.title: Arcane · Ardelia · Liino

Liino brings team ATK, nature amp and healing. Time enemy stacks and combo windows so that Typhi’s energy shots benefit.

showcases.title: Trial – nature stacks and SP rotation
showcases.description: Combat practice team with Typhi, Arcane, Fluorite and Antal. Here the core of energy shots, signs, combo reset and Final Strike SP can be followed particularly clearly.
showcases.rotationAndTips: Position yourself behind the most robust opponent and mark it with Antal. Start with the prepared Hunting Arrows in the Battle Skill until eight signs are ready. Timings of team skills tune to Typhi’s combo so that their new energy shots can immediately consume nature stacks. After that, win back SP via Final Strikes; Dodge Cancels after Final Strike and Landing shorten idle times. For the second burst, trigger team buffs first, then put Typhi's Battle Skill immediately before their Ultimate because of the signature weapon buff. With newly collected signs, start the combo and use the extended air attack window.

showcases.title: Echoes of War – Two Objectives
showcases.description: Two-opponent scenario with Arcane, Ardelia and Liino. Particularly well suited to understanding Typhi’s multi-target attacks and corrosion from natural bursts.
showcases.rotationAndTips: Start with Liino’s Battle Skill for the Team Buff, group the first targets with Arcane and use Typhi’s existing Hunting Arrows. Before the next energy shots, Ardelia’s combo time on the opponents to install corrosion. Liino’s combo helps get back the necessary SP for the next battle skill. Arcane provides more nature stacks in the hovering. Dodge Cancels after airborne landing and Final Strike save time between the two waves.

showcases.title: Nefarith – commented rotation
showcases.description: Full explanation of the Nefarith speed run with team, buff and interrupt timing. The separately published runtime is available in the next showcase.
showcases.rotationAndTips: Prepare buff windows with Xaihi’s Ultimate, Arcane and Liino’s Battle Skill. Typhi then activates the Battle Skill to take the weapon buff with him, using energy shots and the combo reset. In phase two, really avoid the dragon cry and use Final Strikes with Dodge Cancels for SP. Arcanes Battle Skill to time critical interrupt window; Then use Buffs, Nature Stacks, Typhi’s Battle Skill, Arcane Combo and Ultimate in close order. The speed run shown depends on the situation of critical hits.

showcases.title: Nefarith – P0 No Food Speedrun
showcases.description: Stand-alone 0:39 run against Nefarith with Typhoeus P0 and without buff food. For the exact execution and the required critical hits, use the annotated video guide.

showcases.title: Rhodagn – P0 Showcase
showcases.description: Separate Rhodagn Speedrun with Typhi P0. Unlike the Nefarith Run, the video is explicitly designated as a GMS Food Run; Therefore, do not compare maturities without the same conditions.

conclusion.verdict: Typhoeus is a strong and unusually enjoyable Nature main DPS with impressive bursts from her empowered aerial shots and particularly strong damage against two targets. However, she requires a carefully prepared rotation, reliable Nature Infliction stacks and sufficient SP. If your account already has several well-built main DPS operators, Typhoeus is more of a luxury than a necessity.
conclusion.pullAdvice: If you are already well positioned with main DPS operators and pull resources are scarce, you can in good conscience skip Typhi and save for missing roles or future operators. Your signature weapon is a particularly large part of the potential investment. But if you like their hovering and the complex nature burst rotation, you get an independent, very satisfying cause of damage.
recommendedFor: Players who specifically need a nature-main DPS and can reliably prepare nature stacks.
Accounts with Arcane or Fluorite and suitable supporters such as Liino, Ardelia, Perlica or Xaihi.
Players who enjoy challenging air attack rotations, precise buff windows and animation cancels.
Multi-target battles with two opponents against whom their air strikes work particularly well.
skipIf: You already have several invested main DPS operators and need supports more urgently.
You prefer an uncomplicated rotation without Hunting Arrow, Sign and SP management.
You cannot supply reliable Nature Infliction or appropriate buff windows.
conclusion.closingNote: Potentials are nice to have, but never a prerequisite for a functioning P0 rotation. Especially P1 and P5 are strong additives; A new versatile operator can still bring more to your account in the long term. The original September 2026 savings assessment for Si was explicitly a time-bound banner recommendation and is not to be understood as a current release forecast.

overview.summary: Si is a 6★ Cryo Supporter wielding a Greatsword. Her flexible kit allows her to serve as a Combo Skill-focused main DPS, a secondary damage dealer, or a support for Cryo and Heat teams. Artful Intent stores damage taken by an enemy; Inksoul lets your team hit a linked target, while her Ultimate grants Cryo Amp and Heat Amp to the entire team. Getting the most out of her depends on Team Position 01, precise timing and careful SP management.
strengths: Strong personal Cryo Combo Skill damage, crowd control, damage storage, and team-wide Cryo/Heat Amp in one flexible kit.
Fits numerous Cryo and Heat teams while also supporting her own main-DPS rotation.
Inksoul transfers hits and effects to the original target, especially useful when enemies move frequently.
Her talent reduces the Combo Skill cooldown of the operator in Team Position 01 after her Ultimate.
Can apply Cryo Infliction or Heat Infliction depending on the element of the operator in Team Position 01.
weaknesses: Optimizing the Battle Skill sequence, stored damage and Inksoul timing takes practice.
Her strongest new v1.6 gear becomes accessible only late in story progression.
Many of her highest-ceiling team compositions rely on limited operators.
overview.accessibilityNote: The optimal Type 50 equipment parts are only available with the new story and the new area.

operatorKit.playstyle:
Si's kit revolves around Artful Intent and Inksoul. Her initial Battle Skill, Brushwork Realm, deals Cryo DMG, applies Immobilization and Artful Intent, and adds Cryo Infliction. If the operator in Team Position 01 is a Heat operator, the infliction instead becomes Heat Infliction. Artful Intent records a portion of the damage its target takes; when the effect expires, it deals Fixed DMG equal to the stored damage.

After the initial cast, the Battle Skill becomes Initial Stroke (15 SP), which extracts an Inksoul from the marked enemy. Hits and effects applied to the Inksoul also affect its original target. This is particularly useful against moving enemies, because you can concentrate attacks on the Inksoul instead. Final Stroke costs no SP and returns the Inksoul to its host, ending the effect early and triggering the finishing burst. Timing matters: finishing the window too early means less recorded damage.

Her Combo Skill, Fully Envisioned, triggers when an enemy's Cryo Infliction or Heat Infliction is consumed or absorbed. The summoned Ink Lung deals Cryo DMG based on the highest number of Arts Infliction stacks consumed or absorbed from a single target. Prepare those stacks and the reaction window deliberately rather than triggering the Combo Skill at random.

Si's Ultimate, No One Spoils the Fun, deals Cryo DMG and temporarily grants the entire team Cryo Amp and Heat Amp. Proxy's Patronage also temporarily reduces the Combo Skill cooldown of the operator in Team Position 01 after the Ultimate. This makes her a flexible support as well as a Combo Skill-focused main DPS. For damage-focused rotations, prioritize deliberate Combo Skill setups; for support rotations, align her Ultimate with an ally's most important damage window. Before each rotation, check the element in Team Position 01, your available SP, and when to recall the Inksoul.

active.basic: Artistic Urge is Si's five-hit Cryo Basic Attack. When Si is the controlled operator, the final hit contributes 18 Stagger. It is useful for field time and SP recovery in a main DPS build. How highly you level it depends on how often you actually control her; for the core rotation, Combo Skill and Battle Skill come first.
active.battle: Brushwork Realm is Si's control and damage-storage tool. The initial cast applies Artful Intent and either Cryo Infliction or, if a Heat operator occupies Team Position 01, Heat Infliction. Initial Stroke costs 15 SP and extracts an Inksoul; Final Stroke costs no SP and can trigger the finishing explosion early. Leave enough time for attacks and effects to be transferred to the linked enemy before recalling the Inksoul. In a support build, prioritize getting this Battle Skill to M3.
active.combo: Fully Envisioned is Si's primary personal damage source when played as a main DPS. It triggers when Cryo or Heat Infliction stacks are consumed or absorbed. The Ink Lung deals Cryo DMG based on the highest number of stacks removed from a single target. For a main DPS build, level this skill first. Time other team members' Battle Skills carefully to make use of the three-piece Type 50 set bonus.
active.ultimate: No One Spoils the Fun summons an enormous Ink Lung, deals Cryo DMG and grants the entire team Cryo Amp and Heat Amp. Proxy's Patronage then shortens the Combo Skill cooldown of the operator in Team Position 01. As a support, prioritize Battle Skill M3 > Ultimate M3 > Combo Skill M3 > Basic Attack Lv. 1–9 (optional). As main DPS, prioritize Combo Skill M3 > Battle Skill M3 > Basic Attack M3 ≥ Ultimate M3. How frequently you can use the Ultimate depends on your Ultimate Energy efficiency and fight duration.

combatTalents.evaluation: Central Support Talent: After Sis Ultimate, the cooldown of the operator’s combo skill to Team Position 01 is reduced by 10 or 20 seconds. The decisive factors are team order and timing of deployment; can also affect Si itself if it occupies position 1.
If an inksoul disappears, all allied operators receive 15 or 30% haste for five seconds. The free Final Stroke is thus not only the end burst, but also an important team buff timing.

shipTalents.evaluation: Improves the provision of information in the reception room; has no direct significance for Si's combat rotation. Later stages further increase effectiveness.
Slow down the mood decrease of operators in the reception room. It is a base effect, not a fight buff.

recommendations.evaluation: Jade Vessel is valuable as a signature weapon for both Si’s personal cryo/combo damage window and control. After being unable to move, it increases damage to the target and then strengthens the next combo skill; This makes it fit directly with the brushstroke/Inksouln kit.

Long Heritage is a cheaper alternative with matching Intellect/Cryo values. Since release, it has been classified as a Protocol Pass weapon, therefore it is not to be issued as unconditionally free of charge. For specific performance intervals, the Datafield model reference counts.

Khravengger is an alternative run by the official wiki as a suitable large sword option and is designated by Datafield in Si-Main DPS simulations. For the Ultimate reinforcement and the exact team role, jade vessel is still the more specific recommendation.

progression.note: From level 36, Si can enter the cryo and combo focus with Mordvolt Insulation. Prioritize Strength and Intellect on the available parts; Check blueprints in the finder beforehand.
Level 50: further expand with Mordvolt Insulation and Aburrey Flashlight. Starting at Level 60, AIC Fieldwork is another transitional solution.

Level 70: Before unlocking the new v1.6 gear, Early Access with Redeemer Armor and three older Yinglung parts is a full transition build. Once the new area and the corresponding story unlocks are reached, aim for three new Type 50 parts. Redeemer Seal for balanced rotations, LYNX Slab for maximum own damage.

The new version 1.6 Type-50-Yinglung-Set is Sis Go-to-Set. With Redeemer Seal it is balanced, with LYNX Slab aimed at maximum own combo damage. Eternal Xiranite remains a highly situational niche alternative if the set bonus is still missing in the team.

conclusion.verdict: Since her release, Si has proven to be an exceptionally versatile Cryo Supporter who can also serve as a main DPS or sub DPS. My marked Meta teams cover Yvonne, Last Rite, Laevatain and Rossi, as well as Si in the main DPS role. Her strength is not limited to personal Combo Skill damage: control through Inksoul and Artful Intent, alongside buffs for both Cryo and Heat, is equally important. Her basic mechanics are accessible, but optimizing SP timing, reaction windows and team order makes her more demanding.
conclusion.pullAdvice: For accounts with a cryo or heat focus, Si is a particularly interesting addition. Thanks to high flexibility, it can fill various team roles and also enable its own DPS lineup. Jade vessel and Type 50 set are my preferred investment direction, but the new item IDs and the first independent rotation comparisons are not fully confirmed shortly after release. If you only follow maximum own burst numbers, you should compare the final fine tuning with established calculations and your own SP rotation.
recommendedFor: Yvonne and Last Rite teams that benefit from additional Cryo Infliction and Cryo Amp.
Laevatain teams using Heat Infliction through Team Position 01.
Players who want to build Si as a Combo Skill-oriented main DPS.
skipIf: You have no use for Cryo/Heat amplification and cannot obtain her new gear set.
